Summary Description: Dr. Adam Feltz is a psychology researcher at the University of Oklahoma whose work spans numeracy and risk literacy in science communication, climate-change knowledge and risk perception, trust measurement, and applied environmental attitudes. Across multiple studies, he demonstrates a consistent focus on how numeracy and knowledge influence judgments and policy-relevant beliefs, employing rigorous psychometric and structural-modeling approaches (SEM, CFA, EFA, IRT, bootstrapping) and cross-domain applications from climate cognition to trust scale development. His contributions include developing concise, valid measurement instruments (e.g., a four-factor General Interpersonal Trust Scale) and validating their predictive utility in real-world contexts (e.g., recycled water acceptance, animal welfare attitudes, Endangered Species Act attitudes). Committed to open science, Feltz emphasizes cross-sample replication, methodological transparency, and translating theoretical insights into practical tools for research and policy.
